text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government issues White Paper on modernisation of Malta's Armed Forces.

- Association of General Retailers and Traders delegation walks out of technical meeting with government on introduction of new system of indirect taxation. It is not clear what caused the disagreement.

- Public Accounts Committee calls for confiscation of all firearms for which no licence fee has been paid. Auditor-General said thousands of pounds were owed to the government in licences for firearms.
- Father of four goes on trial charged with murdering his wife.
- Paul Sciberras, first president and a founder member of the General Workers Union in 1944, dies.

- Public Broadcasting Services denies discrimination in contract for security services. A private security firm made the claim on Wednesday but PBS said the contract was awarded after a public call for tenders. The tenders were opened in public.

- Court starts hearing case by opposition Nationalist Party against Public Broadcasting Services for alleged discrimination. Party says PBS broadcast meetings between the prime minister and the self-employed on the new system of indirect taxation but refused to give similar treatment to meetings organised by the opposition. The party insists that the constitution demands the state-owned station be unbiased in matters of political controversy.
